title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #2

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

2. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

3. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

4. A — 100 °C

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

6. C — Producers

7. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. A — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

10. B — newton (N)

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Properties of Matter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Conservation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
